sentences.text:
This appeal has been filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) by the claim petitioners in O.P.(MV) No.2413/2010 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Thrissur,
(the Tribunal), aggrieved by the amount of compensation granted by Award dated 08/08/2019.
The respondents herein are respondents 1 to 3 respectively in the petition.
In this appeal, the parties and the documents will be referred to as described in the original petition.

2. According to the claim petitioners, on 05.05.2010 at about 10.30 a.m., while the deceased was Nirmala K.N vs Rajeev K.Job on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61654758/
2 riding his motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KL-48/A-2629 along the Koduvayoor- Pudunagaram public road and when he reached near the place by name Padikkal Padam, goods carrier lorry bearing reg.No.KL- 2025:KER:66460 MACA NO. 963 OF 2020 7/BM-8348, driven by the 2nd respondent in a rash and negligent manner, hit the motorcycle as a result of which he sustained grievous injuries to which he succumbed after 66 days of treatment.
A sum of 10,00,000/- was claimed as compensation under various heads.
3. The 1st respondent/owner and 2nd respondent/ driver filed written statement denying negligence on the part of the latter.
4. The 3rd respondent/insurer filed written statement admitting the existence of a valid policy in respect of the offending vehicle but denied negligence on the part of the second respondent/driver.
The age, occupation and income of the deceased were disputed.
The 2nd respondent/driver did not have a valid driving license and badge at the time of the accident.
It was also contended that the compensation claimed was quite excessive.
5. Before the Tribunal, no oral evidence was adduced by either sides.
Exts.A1 to A12 were marked on the side 2025:KER:66460 MACA NO. 963 OF 2020 of the claim petitioners.
No documentary evidence was produced by the respondents.

6. The Tribunal on consideration of the documentary evidence and after hearing both sides, found negligence on the part of the second respondent/driver of the offending vehicle resulting in the incident and hence awarded an amount of 4,74,305/- together with interest @ 8% per annum from the date of the petition till realisation along with proportionate costs.
Aggrieved by the Award, claim petitioners have come up in appeal.
7. The only point that arises for consideration in this appeal is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.
8. Heard both sides.
9. The award of compensation by the Tribunal under the following heads is challenged by the claim petitioners - Notional income

It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim 2025:KER:66460 MACA NO. 963 OF 2020 petitioners that the notional income of the deceased, an agriculturist, fixed by the Tribunal as 5,000/- is quite low in the light of the dictum in Ramachandrappa v. Manager,
Royal Sundaram Alliance Co. Ltd, (2011) 13 SCC 236 and hence the same needs to be appropriately enhanced.

In case the court is inclined to enhanced the same, the notional income may be fixed as claimed by the claim petitioners, which is 6,000/-.

3 9.1.
It is true that there are no materials produced to show the income of the deceased.

However, in the light of the dictum in Ramachandrappa (Supra), the notional income can be fixed as 7,500/-
per month.
Pain and Suffering 10.
An amount of 1,00,000/- was claimed.
The Tribunal awarded an amount of 40,000/-.
It is submitted by the 2025:KER:66460 MACA NO. 963 OF 2020 learned counsel for the claim petitioners that, after the accident, the deceased had survived for a period of 67 days.
The postmortem certificate shows the extent of injuries sustained in the accident and therefore the amount awarded by the Tribunal under this head may be appropriately enhanced.
Per contra it is submitted by the learned counsel for the 3rd respondent/insurer that, the amount that has been awarded is quite reasonable and that it does not call for any interference.
10.1. The accident took place on 05/05/2010.
The deceased died on 10/07/2010, which is after a period 67 days.
Taking into account the injuries that has been noted in the postmortem certificate, I find that an amount of 55,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.
Loss of earnings 11.
As pointed out earlier, the deceased survived for a period of 67 days.
Therefore, loss of earnings for a period of two months can be awarded.
2025:KER:66460 MACA NO. 963 OF 2020 Multiplier 12.
It is submitted by both sides that the correct multiplier to be applied is 7, whereas, the Tribunal has wrongly applied 5.
Hence, the multiplier to be applied shall be 7.
Extra nourishment 13.
An amount of 3,000/- was claimed.
The Tribunal has not awarded any amount.
Hence, an amount of 3,000/- as claimed under this head can be awarded.

4,74,305/- granted by the Tribunal + 2,53,000 /- granted in appeal) with interest at the rate of 8% per annum from the date of petition till date of realization (excluding the period of 47 days delay in filing the appeal) and proportionate costs.
The third respondent/insurer is directed to deposit the aforesaid amount before the Tribunal within a period of 60 days from the date of receipt of a copy of the judgment.
On deposit of the amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the amount to the claim petitioners at the earliest in accordance with law after making deductions, if any.
